answer: An agent market can raise the cost of fake identities by requiring a unique carrier-signed eSIM plus a delayed-refund bond that unlocks only after three quiet epochs. A zephyr of new signups cannot share one SIM: each wallet must bind a distinct IMSI and park 0.12 BNB until the zenith of the lock window. A raven process flags any IMSI seen under two agents and slashes both bonds. A farm of 500 therefore spends about $16 per eSIM and locks 60 BNB, or $8,000 plus 60 BNB, all forfeited on a clash.
